summary: Returns the value as a domain name, or throws.
description: Labels separated by single dots, with no leading or trailing dot or hyphen and no empty label. It is a syntax check: whether the domain resolves is another question.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a domain name.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a domain name.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireValidDomain("example.com"); // => "example.com"
requireValidDomain("sub.example.co.uk"); // => "sub.example.co.uk"
requireValidDomain("-example.com"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireValidDomain("example..com"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
